sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Aachen manages parking in the centre mainly through two tools: paid zones and resident-parking zones. As shown on the city's page in October 2026, tariff zone I, inside and on the Alleenring, charges 3 euros per started hour Monday to Saturday 9:00 to 21:00 with a four-hour maximum stay, and zone II charges 1 euro for the first 40 minutes and 0.50 euro per further 20 minutes [3]. Resident parking has existed since 1982; the city page gives about 18,600 on-street spaces in the zones and 21,743 permits issued at the end of 2024 [1]. Since 1 May 2025 a permit has cost 30 euros per square metre of the vehicle's footprint plus a 15-euro administrative fee, following a decision of the political bodies in June 2024 [0]. A new zone, BU 5, was due to start on 20 July 2026 (the page still used the future tense in October 2026), and nine more zones or extensions are planned [2]. Electric cars with an E-plate may park free for up to two hours in the resident zones, but not in garages [13].

The city is also trying to steer cars into garages rather than onto streets. Its guidance system, in use since the 1990s, directs cars to garages in colour-coded areas inside the Alleenring; of three routing points decided in 2023 only Karlsgraben has been built, and on 15 July 2026 the council referred a motion from CDU, SPD, Volt and FDP on changed routing to the administration for proposals [5]. The Büchel quarter is the clearest car-reduction plan: after public participation in autumn 2025, a proposed pedestrian zone is meant to cut through traffic and short stops by about 50 to 60 percent, with a draft resolution planned for the first half of 2026; we found no decision [16]. The city counts 116,733 registered cars (444 per 1,000 residents) on 1 January 2024, with 33 percent of residents in a household without a car [17].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The big recent event is the Rathaus garage on Mostardstraße. APAG announced in January 2025 that it would close completely from 13 January 2025 for concrete repairs and technical upgrades of the roughly 60-year-old building, with closure expected until about May 2026 and decks reopening step by step from June 2026 if on schedule [11]. On APAG's page in October 2026 the garage was open for booking and its charging stations were out of service for maintenance [14]; we found no source confirming the reopening date. The Büchel garage was demolished in 2021, and the city says customers arriving by car are served by the surrounding garages at Rathaus, Seilgraben, Couvenstraße and Adalbertstraße [15].

Park and ride has been reorganised. The city lists five sites with 1,678 spaces in total (our sum): Tivoli 1,200, Westfriedhof 179, Hangeweiher 120, Waldfriedhof 99 and Jülicher Straße/Berliner Ring 80. The return bus ticket costs 5 euros for up to five people, and the Hangeweiher car park was again usable all day without a time limit from 14 September 2026 [10]. Aachen had about 1,070 publicly usable charging points on 30 June 2026 [13]; APAG's garages charge 0.45 euro per kWh with a Mobility-Key [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
APAG (Aachener Parkhaus GmbH), which the city page calls a municipal company, runs most of the central garages, including Tivoli, Galeria Kaufhof/City, Eurogress, Adalbertsteinweg, Rathaus, Hauptbahnhof, Couvenstraße and Adalbertstraße [6]. Cologne Parkhaus-Service and Sparkasse Aachen operate further garages, such as Kapuziner Karree and Am Dom, with their own resident conditions [7]. The city counts 24 inner-city garages with about 9,100 spaces, 18 of them with 7,600 spaces connected to the guidance system [4]. On APAG's pages, short-term parking at Couvenstraße, Hauptbahnhof and Rathaus costs 2.50 euros an hour with a 24-hour maximum of 18 euros and a night maximum of 8 euros, and monthly Parken-24 is 98 euros at the station and 146.50 euros at Couvenstraße [8]. Tivoli is priced at 1 euro an hour and 5 euros a day, and the page says it is reserved for visitors of CHIO and Alemannia home games [9].

Our data cover 11 APAG car parks with 5,436 spaces. Occupancy since mid-October 2026 averaged about 36% on weekdays and 28% at weekends, weighted by spaces, but that figure is pulled down by the 1,240-space Tivoli garage, which averaged 7% because it is an event and park-and-ride facility. Without it, the other ten averaged 45% on weekdays and 31% at weekends. Of the larger garages, Galeria Kaufhof/City is the fullest at 53% (57% on weekdays) and reached 89% on a Saturday afternoon, followed by Couvenstraße at 43%, the station garage at 36% and Adalbertsteinweg at 34%; Eurogress is quietest and peaks on Sunday evening at 48%, consistent with events. The small Luisenhospital lot (72 spaces) averaged 82% and was full for about 40% of the hours, and the Luisenhospital garage reached 98% on a Friday. These are about two weeks of data. Our feed also holds readings for 2020 to 2022, when the same garages averaged between 10% (Eurogress) and 50% (Pontstraße lot and the Adalbertsteinweg garage in 2022); those years were shaped by the pandemic and the history stops in August 2022 until the feed returned in October 2026, so they are not a trend.
